measurement_index.name: Traffic
measurement_index.description: BSC traffic measurement (M001) registers information related to the stand alone dedicated control channels (SDCCH) and traffic channels (TCH). The BSC traffic measurement counters are divided into different classes. There are counters regarding the number of attempts to seize TCHs and SDCCHs, successful calls, lengths of the queue, the reasons for Failures and GPRS territory counters. This measurement collects one set of results for each BTS. Signalling charts are drawn with the accuracy of message interface.

measurement_index.name: DFCA
measurement_index.description:
DFCA measurement (M100) collects statistics on the performance of the DFCA. The data is collected at BTS level for each connection type (FR/EFR, HR, 14.4, AMR FR, AMR HR) separately.

When WB-AMR FR codec is in use, AMR FR codec is used in updating counters instead of the WB-AMR FR codec. Separation between WB-AMR FR and AMR FR is not necessary, because the air interface channel coding and the C/I conditions are the same for both of them.

The measurement includes counters for recording the number of DFCA assignments on each C/I level in proportion to the target C/I level, both uplink and downlink. In the same way the statistics on the DFCA estimate amounts are collected: there are separate counters for each most restrictive C/I value in relation to the target C/I value, uplink and downlink.

There are also counters for calculating:
- the total number of successful DFCA assignments
- the number of successful DFCA assignments in high MCMU load situation
- the number of soft blocked DFCA assignments due to C/I and C/N thresholds

measurement_index.name: BSC-BSC
measurement_index.description: BSC-BSC measurement (M102) collects statistics on the inter-BSC communication related to DFCA functionality. The measurement level is BSC, and the measurement objects are identified with a signalling point code (SPC). The counters of this measurement record information on average and peak delay between the Radio Resource Managers in separate BSCs.

measurement_index.name: WPS
measurement_index.description:
WPS Measurement (M103) is related to the Wireless Priority Service (WPS). This measurement is optional (licence-based).

With the counters of WPS Measurement, the user can monitor the performance of traffic channel allocation and queuing algorithms in granting priority access to WPS users.

measurement_index.name: IMSI-based Handover
measurement_index.description:
IMSI-Based Handover (M104) is like a mobile subscriber in a home or visited network can be commanded to measure selectively only cells of specified PLMN areas cells and to make handover accordingly to those specified (home or authorised) PLMNs. The input for the selective measurement control is the PLMN code that is included in the IMSI of the subscriber.

The IMSI-Based Handover measurement is a BTS-level measurement collecting statistics on the IMSI-based HO attempts and failures for each Authorised Network (ANE). There are separate counters for GSM and UTRAN networks.

IMSI-Based Handover supports also software product deactivation which is done automatically when a software product licence has expired. It has been done by changing the state of cell level activation parameters from enabled to disabled.

measurement_index.name: PS DTM
measurement_index.description: PS DTM Measurement (M105) is a BTS-level measurement collecting statistics on Dual Transfer Mode (DTM). It mainly collects network-initiated DTM call establishment information and PS connection-related information of a DTM call.

measurement_index.name: CS DTM
measurement_index.description: CS DTM Measurement (M106) is a BTS-level measurement collecting statistics on Dual Transfer Mode (DTM). It mainly collects MS-initiated DTM call establishment information and CS connection-related information of a DTM call..

measurement_index.name: AMR RX Quality
measurement_index.description:
AMR RX Quality Measurement (M107) collects statistics of received signal quality both in uplink and downlink directions for each AMR bitrate. The information is collected from each transceiver (TRX) separately.

The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels (TCHs). 

The counters that are related to Adaptive Multi Rate (AMR) give information about the distribution of the received signal quality using the different AMR bitrates. There are separate uplink and downlink counters for each RX quality band 0..7 and for full rate as well as for half rate. There are also DL quality counters for Single Antenna Interference (SAIC) capable MSs. There are eight different bitrates (4.75, 5.15, 5.90, 6.70, 7.40, 7.95, 10.2 and 12.2) for AMR FR and five different bitrates (4.75, 5.15, 5.90, 6.70 and 7.40) for AMR HR.

measurement_index.name: DFCA SAIC
measurement_index.description:
DFCA SAIC Measurement (M108) collects statistics on the performance of the DFCA application software for connections of SAIC-capable mobiles. The data is collected at BTS level separately for each connection type (01 = FR / EFR, 02 = HR, 03 = 14.4k HSCSD, 04 = AMR FR / AMR WB, 05 = AMR HR, 08 = DHR, 09 = DFR, 10 = VAMOS DHR and 11 = VAMOS DFR).
 
When WB-AMR FR codec is in use, AMR FR codec is used in updating counters instead of the WB-AMR FR codec. Separation between WB-AMR FR and AMR FR is not necessary, because the air interface channel coding and the C/I conditions are the same for both of them.
 
The measurement includes counters for recording the number of DFCA assignments on each downlink C/I level in proportion to the SAIC-specific C/I target level. In addition, there are also counters for the downlink C/I levels of the most interfered connections in proportion to the SAIC-specific C/I target level.
 
This measurement is optional. Both DFCA and SAIC application software licences need to be activated to run this measurement.

measurement_index.name: Soft Channel Capacity
measurement_index.description:
Soft Channel Capacity measurement (M109) is optional and controlled by a licence.

This measurement type registers information on the availability of traffic channels (TCH) in BCSU object level. The time congestion of TCHs and the average and peak numbers of busy TCHs are measured. The collected information is sampled for averaging at certain intervals. This sampling interval for the defined counters is 20 seconds for some statistical items that are averaged. Thus the actual value of this measurement contains averaged information collected within a measurement period. The Soft Channel Capacity measurement collects one set of results for BCSU logical address

measurement_index.name: PCU Utilisation
measurement_index.description: PCU Utilization Measurement (M110) records the peak number of used channels in UL/DL direction per PCU and the number of occupied packet data traffic channels (PDTCH) per PCU.

measurement_index.name: AMR Progressive Power Control
measurement_index.description: AMR Progressive Power Control Measurement (M111) measures the RX quality class according to the distribution of the transmitting power class. There are four counters for each transmitting power class (0-15). The measurement has separate RX quality counters for uplink and downlink. Every RX quality counter has a denominator counter that indicates the number of times the RX quality class sum counter is sampled. The counters are updated only in case of AMR FR and AMR HR calls

measurement_index.name: AMR Signalling
measurement_index.description: AMR Signalling measurement (M112) measures a proportion of repeated ACCH capable mobiles in the network and usage of repeated SACCH and FACCH features.

measurement_index.name: Power Saving
measurement_index.description: Power Saving Measurement (M113) measures the cumulative idle time of power reduced dedicated channels in the circuit-switched territory of the BCCH TRX and the use of full BCCH power and reduced output power in connections of a BCCH TRX. In addition cumulative downtime for powered-down dual TRXs is measured.

measurement_index.name: Pseudo Wire BSC
measurement_index.description:
Pseudo Wire BSC Measurement (M114) reports performance data about the pseudo wire functionality in the BSC. The data is reported at the PSN tunnel + Pseudo Wire level. The data is collected from every active Exchange Terminal for IP Transmission unit (ETIP) under the BSC supervision, including the A-interface ETIP units combined in the TCSM3i configuration..
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: Ethernet BSC
measurement_index.description:
Ethernet BSC Measurement (M115) reports performance data about the availability and quality of the Ethernet interfaces of the Exchange Terminal for IP transmission units (ETIP) under BSC supervision. The data is reported in Ethernet interface level. The data is collected from every active ETIP unit under BSC supervision including A-interface ETIP units in TCSM3i Combi configuration.

Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: Pseudo Wire TCSM
measurement_index.description:
Pseudo Wire TCSM Measurement (M116) reports performance data about the pseudo wire functionality in the TCSM. The data is reported at the PSN tunnel + Pseudo Wire level. The data is collected from the active Aterinterface and the A-interface Exchange Terminal for IP Transmission units (ETIP) under the supervision of the standalone TCSM3i.
.
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: Ethernet TCSM
measurement_index.description:
Ethernet TCSM Measurement (M117) reports performance data about the availability and quality of the Ethernet interfaces in active Exchange Terminal for IP transmission units (ETIP) under standalone TCSM supervision. The data is reported in Ethernet interface level. The data is collected from Ater-interface and A-interface ETIP unit under standalone TCSM supervision.

Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: Pseudo Wire Tunnel BTS
measurement_index.description:
Pseudo Wire Tunnel BTS Measurement (M118) reports performance data about the Pseudo Wire (PW) functionality in the BTS and BTS supervised units in the PW mode. The data is collected from every unit in the PW mode under the BTS supervision.

Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: TRE Ethernet
measurement_index.description: TRE Ethernet Measurement (M119) reports performance data about the functionality of the Ethernet interface in a BTS. The data is collected from every BTS with a transport plug-in unit supporting Ethernet transport interface.

measurement_index.name: TDM/PW Abis Delay
measurement_index.description:
TDM/PW Abis Delay Measurement (M120) provides performance data about the round trip time of data frames/packets in an Abis interface. The measurement supports TDM and pseudo wire emulation edge to edge (PWE3) transmission techniques. In case of integrated pseudo wire equipment solution, jitter buffer fill level data is provided by BTS and exchange terminal for IP transmission(ETIP) unit at the BSC end of the connection.
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: Circuit-switched Dynamic Abis Pool
measurement_index.description:
Circuit-switched Dynamic Abis Pool measurement (M121) reports Performance Measurement data about Circuit-switched Dynamic Abis Pool (CSDAP) usage rate. It enables operator to optimize the size of CSDAP. The data is reported in CSDAP ID level.
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

The counters shall also be updated in case of Remote CSDAP.

measurement_index.name: OSC RX Quality
measurement_index.description:
OSC RX Quality Measurement (M122) collects statistics of received signal quality both in uplink and downlink directions for each AMR HR bitrate for double half rate calls and AMR FR bitrate for double full rate calls. The information is collected from each transceiver separately.
The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels.
The counters that are related to Double Half Rate and OSC Full Rate gives information about the distribution of the received signal quality using the different AMR bitrates. There are separate uplink and downlink counters for each RX quality band 0..7 and for each AMR bitrate used with a double half rate call and double full rate call. There are five different bitrates for Double Half Rate and eight different bitrates for OSC Full Rate.

measurement_index.name: Packet Abis BTS
measurement_index.description: Packet Abis BTS measurement (M123) reports Abis U-plane and SCTP statistics provided by BTS. This measurement includes counters which reports information on number of frames, octets, RTP and UDP packets sent/received. This measurement also gives information about the utilization of uplink and downlink bandwidth.

measurement_index.name: Packet Abis Traffic
measurement_index.description: Packet Abis Traffic measurement (M124) reports Abis U-plane statistics provided by functional ETP Units under BSC supervision. The counters of this measurement give information about the number of uplink and downlink RTP and UDP packets or octets of CS/PS Uplane. In addition, counters of this measurement report whether the packets are received on time according to the timestamp.

measurement_index.name: Packet Abis SCTP
measurement_index.description: Packet Abis SCTP measurement (M125) reports M- and C-plane SCTP statistics are provided by Platform software in BCSU/BCXU. Packet Abis over Ethernet or Packet Abis over TDM license is required to be able to activate this measurement type.

measurement_index.name: Packet Abis Delay
measurement_index.description: Packet Abis Delay measurement (M126) reports Abis delay statistics provided by BTS. Measurement data is collected from all BCFs using Packet Abis over Ethernet or Packet Abis over TDM features. The counters of this measurement report information about roundtrip time.

measurement_index.name: Packet Abis Congestion Control
measurement_index.description: Packet Abis Congestion Control measurement (M127) reports congestion control actions. The measurement data is reported in BCF level. The counters of this measurement gives information about the duration of congestion control and overload action of new circuit switched and packet switched calls.

measurement_index.name: ETP Ethernet BSC
measurement_index.description:
ETP Ethernet BSC measurement (M128) reports ethernet level statistics provided by functional ETP Units under BSC supervision at active external Ethernet interface level. Typically this measurement collects counters from ETPA, ETPE and ETPT units. The counters of this measurement reports information about the number of transmitted Ethernet frames [errored and non-errored] and the number of transmitted octets in valid Ethernet frames.

Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: ETP Ethernet TCSM
measurement_index.description: ETP Ethernet TCSM (M129) is obsolete

measurement_index.name: Undefined Adjacent Cell
measurement_index.description: Undefined adjacent cell measurement (M013) registers statistics on cells which have not been defined as adjacent cells but which are among those six neighbouring cells that the MS receives best. This measurement type collects one set of results for each BTS.

measurement_index.name: AoIP Traffic BSC
measurement_index.description: AoIP Traffic BSC measurement (M130) reports A and Ater interface statistics provided by ETP unit controlled by BSC. This measurement collects counters from ETPA and ETMA units.

measurement_index.name: AoIP Traffic TCSM
measurement_index.description: AoIP Traffic TCSM (M131) is obsolete

measurement_index.name: Local Switching Traffic
measurement_index.description:
Local Switching Traffic measurement (M132) reports CS U-Plane RTP and UDP packets for each BTS configured to Packet Abis BCF Group. The counters of this measurement gives information about the number of transmitted uplink and downlink RTP, UDP packets/octets of CS U-plane. 
In addition, counters of this measurement reports whether the packets received too early or received too late according to the timestamp.

measurement_index.name: Ethernet mcTC
measurement_index.description: Ethernet mcTC (M133) is obsolete

measurement_index.name: Ethernet mcBSC
measurement_index.description: Ethernet mcBSC measurement (M134) reports Ethernet level statistics provided by Ethernet switch of mcBSC. The counters of this measurement reports information about the number of received/transmitted Ethernet frames [errored and non-errored] and the number of received/transmitted octets in valid Ethernet frames.

measurement_index.name: Precise RX Level
measurement_index.description: Precise RX Level Measurement (M135) collects the statistics of the uplink and downlink RX signal level. The counters are incremented according to the number of each RX level class received by the BSC in the radio link measurement result messages. The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH only. The rx level is divided into 64 levels from -110 dBm to -48 dBm in a step of 1 dBm.

measurement_index.name: Precise Timing Advance
measurement_index.description: Precise Timing Advance Measurement (M136) registers information on the timing advance during calls. Timing Advance (TA) value in measurement result is from 0 to 63. One TA value is equal to 550 metre. Each TA value in the measurement result is recorded in the counter. The information is collected for each TRX. The counters are incremented according to the number of each TA values received by the BSC in the radio link measurement result messages. The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH.

measurement_index.name: Precise Power Level
measurement_index.description: Precise Power Level Measurement (M137) reports transmission power level of mobile station and base station. The counters are incremented according to the number of each Power level received by the BSC in the radio link measurement result messages. The counters are collected for each TRX. There are 39 counters in this measurement. 23 counters for MS power level and 16 for Base station power level. The power levels of the BTS are relative to the maximum transmission power of the BTS with a step of -2 dBm. The counters of this measurement are updated both on TCH and on SDCCH.

measurement_index.name: Adjacent Cell RX Level
measurement_index.description:
Adjacent Cell RX Level Measurement (M138) reports different RX level statistics of adjacent cell with respect to the serving cell. The 4 kind of counters in this measurement are Adjacent cell RX Level Rank, Adjacent cell RX levels, Serving-adjacent RX level difference and Serving-Adjacent RX level matrix. The counters are incremented according to the number of each RX level received by the BSC in the radio link measurement result messages. This measurement is collected for the combination of a serving cell and an adjacent cell. The adjacent cells can be defined or undefined. The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH. Adjacent cell RX level Rank has 3 counters. These rank counters are to find the strongest 3 adjacent cells.
Adjacent RX level has 64 counters. The Adjacent RX level is divided into 64 levels from -110 dBm to -48 dBm in a step of 1 dBm.
Serving-Adjacent cell RX level difference has 51 counters. The difference of serving cell RX level and Adjacent cell RX level are defined as 51 levels. The 51 levels are from -24 dBm to +24 dBm in a step of 1 dBm.
Serving-Adjacent cell RX level matrix has 121 counters. The RX level of serving cell and adjacent cell are classified to 11 levels.
RX_LEVEL_0 -100dBm > rx_lev,
RX_LEVEL_1 -95dBm > rx_lev>= -100dBm,
RX_LEVEL_2 -90dBm > rx_lev>= -95dBm,
RX_LEVEL_3 -85dBm > rx_lev>= -90dBm,
RX_LEVEL_4 -80dBm > rx_lev>= -85dBm,
RX_LEVEL_5 -75dBm > rx_lev>= -80dBm,
RX_LEVEL_6 -70dBm > rx_lev>= -75dBm,
RX_LEVEL_7 -65dBm > rx_lev>= -70dBm,
RX_LEVEL_8 -60dBm > rx_lev>= -65dBm,
RX_LEVEL_9 -55dBm > rx_lev>= -60dBm,
RX_LEVEL_10 rx_lev>= -55dBm.
In each measurement result, the RX levels of the adjacent cell and serving cell is plotted against each of these bands. For the combination of 11 levels of RX levels of serving and adjacent, there are 121 counters.
Example:
If the range of Serving Cell RxLevel = -79 dBm and RxLevel Ncell 0 = -91 dBm, the counter 138174, SERVING-ADJACENT RX LEVEL MATRIX 56 will be updated.

measurement_index.name: Air Path Loss
measurement_index.description:
Air Path Loss Measurement (M139) collects the data of uplink, downlink and path loss difference between the uplink and downlink.
Air Path Loss Measurement measures the number of samples (both in DL and UL direction) per certain criteria. This measurement has 176 counters, which are 65 for DL and 60 for UL and 51 for the difference between the UL and DL path loss. The counters are updated to corresponding classes per uplink, downlink and path loss difference between uplink and downlink.

measurement_index.name: RX Quality Statistics
measurement_index.description:
RX Quality Statistics Measurement (M014) registers received signal quality information both in uplink and downlink directions. The information is collected from each transceiver (TRX) separately.

The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The counters give the distribution of these samples divided to each quality band. There are also DL quality counters for Single Antenna Interference (SAIC) capable MSs.The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels (TCHs).

The counters that are related to Adaptive Multi Rate (AMR) codecs give information about the distribution of the received signal quality using the different AMR codec modes. There are separate uplink and downlink counters for each RX quality band 0..7 and for full rate codec modes 1..4 as well as half rate codec modes 1..4. There is also a counter (014149) that provides information about the actual AMR codecs used in the mode sets during the measurement period. An interpretation of this counter is given in AMR Mode Set decoding (Counter 014149).

measurement_index.name: Multipoint A
measurement_index.description: Multipoint A (M141) interface feature has several options to select the SPC for a call. The counters in this measurement helps to know which option in Multipoint A interface feature has been used to select an SPC for the call. These counters are known in A-interface. Sum of first six counters indicates overall amount of connections created towards concerned SPC in measurement period. The other two counters are updated always according to Load Balancing criteria and when NAS Node Selection was used.

measurement_index.name: Antenna
measurement_index.description:
Antenna measurement (M142) collects counters of Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR) and Received Signal Strength Indication (RSSI). VSWR and RSSI values are collected for detecting antenna and cable system problems. BTS collects the RSSI counters for each TRX and its association to Main and Diversity Antennas, and VSWR counters from each antenna of the BTSs.
 
When 2-way diversity is in use, RSSI counters are reported for main and 1st diversity antenna (Antenna type values are 0 and 1 respectively). If the 4-way diversity is in use, RSSI counters are reported for the diversity antennas two and three (Antenna type values 2 and 3), otherwise not reported for those antennas. RSSI value is accepted as valid if Rx level of received Circuit Switched channel burst is above the defined limit value. The reliable RSSI condition is fulfilled when the limit defined in the parameter RX difference Samples Count of valid RSSI samples for a hour exceeds.
 
VSWR counters are reported for each antenna when values are valid. VSWR values are not reported when invalid VSWR and low TX Power alarms are triggered.

measurement_index.name: MOCN CS
measurement_index.description: RG301777 Multi Operator Core Network (M146) allows several operators to share the radio access network resources as spectrum, cells and BSC between Core Network operators. The operators can have a joint venture which operates the shared radio access network and the shared network which has own OSS. MOCN CS Measurement collects counters related to Multi Operator Core Network (MOCN) selection for CS (Circuit Switched) access and registers information of CS attempts, rejections and rerouting events on Operator ID and Segment ID level.

measurement_index.name: MOCN PS
measurement_index.description: RG301777 Multi Operator Core Network (M147) allows several operators to share the radio access network resources as spectrum, cells and BSC between Core Network operators. The operators can have a joint venture which operates the shared radio access network and the shared network which has own OSS. MOCN PS Measurement collects counters related to Multi Operator Core Network (MOCN) selection for Packet Switched (PS) access. MOCN PS Measurement registers information of PS attempts, rejections and rerouting events on Operator Id and Segment Id level.

measurement_index.name: Node RX Quality and RX Level
measurement_index.description: Node RxQuality and RxLevel Measurement (M148) reports the received signal quality and signal level information both in uplink and downlink directions for the node of the composite cell (CMST).The RX Quality part registers received signal quality information. The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The counters give the distribution of these samples divided to each quality band. The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels (TCHs).The RX level part registers information on the level and quality of RX signal. The RX level is provided in six subclasses per RX quality band in both uplink and downlink directions. There are 48 counters corresponding to the RX quality bands defined in both uplink and downlink directions. The incrementation is made according to the number of each RX level class received by the BSC in the radio link measurement messages. RX level is divided into six subclasses in both uplink and downlink measurements and the ranges of the classes are set by the user with the RXn parameter of the measurement 53 RX Level Statistics, for example 0-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-30, 31-40, 41-63. In the RX level counter incrementation the missing radio downlink measurement reports and the BTS measurement averaging parameter are taken into account. If the downlink measurement is missing, the latest downlink measurement is used. This way the counters are updated every 480 ms.

measurement_index.name: Node Handover Adjacent Cell
measurement_index.description: Node Handover Adjacent Cell Measurement (M149) collects counters about how handovers between different cells are divided. Counters are updated when the handover is performed to the adjacent cells from the node of the serving Composited Multisite Transmission (CMST) cell. Counters are collected for maximum 78 adjacent cells. One set of counters are collected for adjacent cells if more than 78 adjacent cells are recorded during the measurement period. BTS and Node identifications of the serving CMST cell are in the measurement header object part and adjacent cell identifications are in the counter part. The measurement includes counters for handover attempts, successful handovers, and counters for failed handovers.

measurement_index.name: Handover Adjacent Cell
measurement_index.description:
Handover Adjacent Cell Measurement (M015) collects statistics about how handovers between different cells are divided. The measurement includes counters for handover attempts, successful handovers, and counters for failed handovers due to lack of radio resources.

The counters are grouped into four categories:

- The internal intra-cell handovers are collected into the adjacent cell 0 counters 015000-015006.

- The primary counters for inter-cell handovers in BSC; the first 32 requests for internal inter-cell handovers in BSC or external handovers in BSC during a measurement period are collected by the primary adjacent cell 1-32 counters 015007-015230.

- The primary counters for inter-cell handovers in BSC; the next 32 requests for internal inter-cell handovers in BSC or external handovers in BSC during a measurement period are collected by the primary adjacent cell 33-64 counters 015270-015493.

- The secondary counters for inter-cell handovers in BSC. If there are requests for internal inter-cell handovers in BSC or external handovers in BSC to/from more than 64 adjacent cells during a measurement period, the rest of the requests are summed to the secondary undefined adjacent cell counters 015231-015237.

- The PLMN information counters are updated together with the LAC/CI information of the primary counters.

measurement_index.name: Node Traffic
measurement_index.description: Node Traffic Measurement (M150) collects TCH assignments and failures, and TBF establishments and failures for both uplink and downlink. Node is one remote radio head module in one physical location of Remote Radio Head chain (RRH), belonging to one Composited Multisite Transmission (CMST). Counters are collected for CMST cell. This measurement can be activated only if the corresponding ON/OFF license Node Level PM for CMST cell is enabled.

measurement_index.name: BSS Top PhaseSync
measurement_index.description: BSS ToP PhaseSync Measurement (M151) collects information as error times, service level and messages of Timing over Packet phase synchronization per BCF. Via these measurement counters operator can monitor phase stability in the BSS network.

measurement_index.name: Beam RX Quality and RX Level
measurement_index.description:
Bean Rx Quality and Rx Level Measurement (M152) reports the received signal quality and signal level information both in uplink and downlink directions for the beam of TRX.
The RX Quality part registers received signal quality information. The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The counters give the distribution of these samples divided to each quality band. The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels (TCHs).
The RX level part registers information on the level and quality of RX signal. There are 48 counters corresponding to the RX quality bands defined in both uplink and downlink directions. The incrementation is made according to the number of each RX level class received by the BSC in the radio link measurement messages. RX level is divided into six subclasses in both uplink and downlink measurements and the ranges of the classes are set by the user with the RXn parameter of the measurement 53 RX Level Statistics, for example 0-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-30, 31-40, 41-. In the RX level counter incrementation the missing radio downlink measurement reports and the BTS measurement averaging parameter are taken into account. If the downlink measurement is missing, the latest downlink measurement is used. This way the counters are updated every 480 ms.

measurement_index.name: Extended Coverage GSM IoT
measurement_index.description:
EC-GSM IoT Measurement (M153) reports statistics in EC-GSM IoT enabled BTS and coverage class level.
In EC-GSM IoT Measurement Coverage Class mapping 
- UL TBF counters shall be updated with used UL CC. Counter shall be mapped for    BTS/CC object accordingly. 
- DL TBF counters shall be updated with used DL CC. Counter shall be mapped for BTS/CC object accordingly. 
- If CC is not available or not relevant for counter (like EC DL TBF PER TIMESLOT), counter shall be mapped for BTS/CC1 object.

measurement_index.name: POWER EFFICIENT OPERATION
measurement_index.description: PEO Measurement (M154) reports PEO statistics in PEO feature license is in ON state.

measurement_index.name: EC-GSM IoT Enhanced
measurement_index.description: EC-GSM IoT Enhanced Measurement (M155) reports statistics in EC_EGPRS feature license is in ON state.

measurement_index.name: AoIP traffic MultiOperator BSC
measurement_index.description: AoIP Traffic BSC measurement (M156) reports A and Ater interface statistics provided by ETP unit controlled by BSC. This measurement collects operator specific counters from ETPA and ETMA units.

measurement_index.name: MOCN Enhanced
measurement_index.description: MOCN Enhanced Measurement (M157) registers the statistics per operator which include counters for circuit switched(CS) voice calls, Short messaging Services(SMS) and Supplementary Services.

measurement_index.name: SDCCH Observation
measurement_index.description: SDCCH observation (M016) contains information on the seizure and release of the channel. The observations are collected at the channel level.

measurement_index.name: TCH Observation
measurement_index.description: TCH observation (M017) contains detailed information on the seizure and release of one TCH. The observations are collected at the channel level.

measurement_index.name: Internal Handover Observation
measurement_index.description: Internal handovers observation (M018) contains information on different types of handovers: identifications of the source and target base station transceivers (BTS), duration of the handover, handover cause, phase in or out, and channel type or number. The observation is collected at the BTS level. The direction of the handover is determined in its relation to the BSC.

measurement_index.name: Incoming Handover Observation
measurement_index.description: Incoming handovers observation (M019) contains information on different types of handovers: identifications of the source and target base station transceivers (BTS), duration of the handover, handover cause, phase in or out, and channel type or number. The observation is collected at the BTS level. The direction of the handover is determined in its relation to the BSC.

measurement_index.name: Resource Availability
measurement_index.description:
Resource Availability (M002) registers information on the availability of traffic channels (TCH), the stand-alone dedicated control channels (SDCCH), broadcast control channels (BCCH) and timeslots. 

It also collects information on the availability of the TCHs for each interference band. In addition, time congestion of TCHs and SDCCHs, and the average and peak numbers of busy TCHs or SDCCHs are measured.

The collected information is sampled for averaging at certain intervals. This sampling interval for the defined counters is 20 seconds for statistical items that are averaged. Thus the actual value of this measurement contains averaged information collected within a measurement period. The Resource Availability measurement collects one set of results for each BTS.

measurement_index.name: Outgoing Handover Observation
measurement_index.description: Outgoing handovers observation (M020) contains information on different types of handovers: identifications of the source and target base station transceivers (BTS), duration of the handover, handover cause, phase in or out, and channel type or number. The observation is collected at the BTS level. The direction of the handover is determined in its relation to the BSC.

measurement_index.name: Radio Measurement Report
measurement_index.description:
Radio Measurement Reports (M021) counters provide detailed information on handovers made during the call as well as levels and qualities of the uplink and downlink signals and the signal levels received by the 6 adjacent cells (the 15 adjacent cells when Enhanced Measurement Report is in use). The information collected from the calls is presented in the following groups:
- uplink measurement results 
- downlink measurement results
- adjacent cell measurement results.

All this information is sent directly to the network management system (NMS) using events through the Q3 interface. The information is available online in the NMS. This observation can be activated only from the NMS.

measurement_index.name: Clear Code Observation
measurement_index.description:
Clear Code Observation (M022) contains information on the clear codes that indicate a failure in a call. The failure may lead to call dropping or inform about handover problems.

There are two alternative ways of focusing the observation and making the clear code observation an efficient tool: finding all failure codes in one BTS or finding one clear code in all BTSs under one BSC.

measurement_index.name: Abis D-channel
measurement_index.description:
Abis D-channel Measurement (M226) The Abis D-channel measurement provides information on the end-to-end performance of the Abis transmission connection. It includes information on framing errors and transmitted octets together with uplink UI and I frame information of Abis D-channels.

When Abis LAPD multiplexing is used with the BTSPlus, counters cannot be collected per each single multiplexed D-channel separately. Instead, one of the D-channels acts as a master channel and the statistics of all the multiplexed D-channels are collected on that channel.

measurement_index.name: Dropped Call Observation
measurement_index.description:
Dropped Call Observation (M024) contains detailed information on a call that has dropped possibly due to some failure.

A new set of records containing data on the last few seconds of a call is added to the observation file every time the call has dropped due to some cause that is recognised as a call drop.

measurement_index.name: TBF Observation for GPRS Trace
measurement_index.description:
TBF Observation for GPRS Trace (M025) is a part of the System Level Trace for GPRS. It also expands the tracing capabilities to packet switched services.

TBF Observation for GPRS Trace observes two events and registers them in the counters:

- resource consumption by the subscriber during tracing, which includes allocations, reallocations and releases of Temporary Block Flows (TBF)
- call quality related transactions performed on the subscriber, which consist of changes in the used coding scheme and MS flow control.

The System Level Trace for GPRS in BSC is activated by a message from the SGSN.

measurement_index.name: GPRS Cell Re-selection Report
measurement_index.description:
GPRS Cell Re-selection (M027) is a new trace report for GPRS trace. It contains information about NCCR triggering, NACC usage and possible failures.

Report is closed and sent further to NetAct when flush is received from SGSN, MS returns to source cell by Packet cell change failure, or NCCR context is released in PCU.

measurement_index.name: GPRS RX Level and Quality Report
measurement_index.description:
GPRS RX Level and Quality Report (M028) is a report type needed to record serving and neighbour cell measurements and quality data. This report contains the following information:
- downlink RX level of serving cell and neighbour cells from packet (enhanced) measurement report
- downlink RX quality class or BEP values from (EGPRS) Packet downlink acknowledgement message
- uplink RX level and quality from BTS measurements.

measurement_index.name: Drop Call Breakdown Observation
measurement_index.description:
Drop Call Breakdown observation (M029) collects statistics on the dropped calls. The detailed data of drop is collected when the drop occurs after the ASSIGNMENT_COMPLETE message. The focus of the observation can be either the breakdown of counter DROP AFTER TCH ASSIGN or the breakdown of counter CLEAR REQUEST SENT BY BSC ON TCH.

If the focus of the observation is breakdown of DROP AFTER TCH ASSIGN, the observation data is reported when the TCH drop occurred between messages ASSIGNMENT_COMPLETE from BTS and DISCONNECT from MS/MSC. If the focus of the observation is breakdown of CLEAR REQUEST SENT BY BSC ON TCH, the observation data is reported when CLEAR_REQUEST message is sent to MSC between the ASSIGNMENT_COMPLETE from BTS and CLEAR_COMMAND from MSC messages.

The observation is activated on BSC level and drops are recorded per TRX. The Drop Call Breakdown Observation data is stored to an observation report disk file and sent to NetAct in an observation file.

measurement_index.name: Resource Access
measurement_index.description: Resource Access (M003) Measurement registers information on all common control channels (CCCH) of the base station controller. The recorded items of data comprise the number of messages sent to the Abis interface. The messages are sorted according to message type, average load on control channels, and the number of traffic channel seizures for mobile originating (MOC) and terminating calls (MTC). Signalling charts are drawn with the accuracy of message interface.

measurement_index.name: Position-based Services Observation
measurement_index.description:
Position Based Services (PBS) (M030) is used to locate valid mobile equipment. Position calculation can be done in the Internal SMLC or the External SMLC. The PBS observation collects detailed information from the positioning calculation procedure.

The location methods in the Internal SMLC are Cell ID+TA and Conventional GPS. The METHOD_USED counter of the observation shows the used location methods during the positioning calculation procedure. The External SMLC can be connected to the BSC via an Lb-interface and can include other position methods than Internal SMLC. The SMLC_USED counter of the observation shows which SMLC is used to perform position calculation. The observation report is collected for each location procedure of the mobile equipment located in the target cell for the observation.

measurement_index.name: CS L3 Message Observation
measurement_index.description: CS L3 Message Observation (M031) contains information of transferred L3 messages of Circuit Switched (CS) connections on Abis and A interfaces. CS L3 Message observation can be activated on LAC-CI, BTS, TRX or TSL level or report is generated for the traced user, or observed mobiles or equipments.

measurement_index.name: Handover
measurement_index.description: Handover measurement (M004) registers information about the number of handovers (HO) controlled by the mobile switching centre (MSC) or the base station controller (BSC). The recorded items of data comprise the number of the incoming, outgoing, or intra-cell HOs, and the number of successful and unsuccessful attempts, seizures, and HOs. The HOs are sorted according to direction, where appropriate. This measurement type collects one set of results for each BTS. Signalling charts are drawn with the accuracy of message interface.

measurement_index.name: Power Control
measurement_index.description:
Power Control (M005) registers information on how the BSC controls the power level and signal quality of the mobile station (MS) and the base transceiver station (BTS). It allows the user to obtain information on the number of power control messages which the BSC sends to the MS and the BTS, and on the quality and strength of the signals both in uplink and downlink direction. This measurement collects one set of results for each TRX.

A TRX-level object is a combination of BTS, TRX, and radio frequency numbers. Exceeding the maximum number of objects, for example, radio network configuration changes within a measurement period, causes missed counter updates and the "STATISTICS: too much objects" log writing to the MCMU log.

The counters of this measurement are updated both on TCH and on SDCCH.

measurement_index.name: BSC Level Clear Code
measurement_index.description:
BSC Level Clear Code Measurement (M050) record failures that have occurred during a call (signalling or conversation). The measurement collects the clear code counters for each of the 15 call phases (see Call phases of Call related DX Causes in BSC in Call related DX Causes in BSC under Reference/Clear codes\cause codes in the PDF view). The values of all counters are given on a BSC basis.

Each counter has a corresponding failure DX cause, whose cause number is the same as the last three digits of the counter number. For example, the clear code counter 0500315 CONN FAIL corresponds to the failure DX cause conn_fail_c (315). For a complete list of the failure DX causes, see List of call related DX causes in BSC in Call related DX Causes.

measurement_index.name: BSC Level Clear Code (PM)
measurement_index.description:
BSC Level Clear Code (PM) Measurement (M051) counters are divided into five different classes; there are failure counters, success counters, one BCSU/BCXU counter, call attempt and call establishment cause counters, and handover counters. The failure and success counters together characterize the quality of service. All counters are given on BSC basis.

Most of the counters have a one-to-one correspondence with a particular DX cause. These correspondences are indicated in the counter descriptions. However, some of the counters are primarily based on 3GPP-based BSSMAP causes or establishment causes. In those cases, the name of the BSSMAP cause or establishment cause is also mentioned in the counter descriptions

measurement_index.name: STM-1 Interface
measurement_index.description:
STM-1 Interface Measurement (M513) The STM-1 Interface Measurement monitors the ability of different hierarchical levels of SDH/SONET connection to provide agreed quality at the speed of STM-1/OC-3 per SDH/SONET Exchange Terminal (SET). The measurement provides information about the amount of Errored Background Blocks (EBB), amount of Errored Seconds (ES), amount of Severely Errored Seconds (SES), and amount of Unavailable Seconds (UAS). The measurement counters are collected from the SDH/SONET termination equipment on physical interface (SET). The measurement identifier is 513/201H.

The object is SDH/SONET exchange terminal (SET) that is identified by the exchange terminal type (SET) and index. There are also counters for SDH/SONET paths terminated to a certain SDH/SONET exchange terminal. In case VC-12 over VC-4 mapping is used, the STM-1/OC-3 interface contains one path, the counters of PATH1 are updated and others are left to zero. In case VC-12 over VC-3 or VC-11 over VC-3 / VT1.5 over STS-1 mapping is used, the STM-1/OC-3 interface contains three paths and all path counters are updated. n be used.

There is a restriction in defects that effect far-end counters. If there is a near-end SES caused by near-end defect then far-end path at same stage is assumed error free. This is because the far-end error indications and counts got from SDH/SONET frame are possibly corrupted because of near-end defects.

In case the terminology is different according to the regulations of American National Standards Institute (ANSI) and European Telecommunications Standards Institute (ETSI), both ANSI and ETSI versions are used in the document, divided with '/' (for example, STM-1/OC-3).

measurement_index.name: SONET/SDH Protection Group
measurement_index.description:
SONET/SDH Protection Group Measurement (M516) This measurement monitors the usage of protection groups configured for SONET or SDH transmission sections. The statistics can be used to follow transmission network quality.

The object of the measurement is protection group of SDH/SONET exchange terminal that is identified by the Protection group ID.

measurement_index.name: Underlay-Overlay Statistics
measurement_index.description:
Underlay-overlay statistics measurement (M052) registers information on the performance of this software. Statistics are compiled in counters reserved for each TRX. Measurements are not reference group specific.

The information of the underlay-overlay statistics measurement is divided into different parts. Signalling charts are drawn with the accuracy of message interface.

In the underlay-overlay statistics measurement the maximum number of TRX- level statistic objects is 3000. A TRX level object is a combination of BTS, TRX, and radio frequency numbers. Exceeding of the maximum number of the objects, for example, radio network configuration changes within a measurement period causes missed counter updates and the "STATISTICS: too much objects" log writing to the MCMU log.

The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH only.

measurement_index.name: RX Level Statistics
measurement_index.description:
RX Level Statistics (M053) registers information on the level and quality of RX signal on both uplink and downlink direction.

This measurement provides the network operator with the RX level in six classes per RX quality band in both uplink and downlink directions. The measurement for the RX level statistics consists of 96 counters. There are 48 counters corresponding to the RX quality bands defined in both uplink and downlink directions. The incrementation is made according to the number of each RX level class received by the BSC in the radio link measurement messages. RX level is divided into six subclasses in both uplink and downlink measurements and the ranges of the classes are set by the user, for example 0-10, 11-15, 16-20, 21-30, 31-40, 41-63. In the RX level counter incrementation the missing radio downlink measurement reports and the BTS measurement averaging parameter are taken into account. If the downlink measurement is missing, the latest downlink measurement is used. This way the counters are updated every 480 ms.

measurement_index.name: Resource Availability per BSC
measurement_index.description:
Resource availability per BSC (M056) registers information on the availability of the transceivers (TRXs) on the BSC level. The number of the TRXs which are not available is divided into three categories according to what causes the unavailability:
- the user
- internal reasons
- external reasons.

The counters of the resource availability per BSC measurement are sampled every 20 seconds.

measurement_index.name: BSC Level Clear Code (SERLEV)
measurement_index.description: BSC Level Clear Code (SERLEV) Measurement (M057) registers statistics about clear codes in a BSC during calls. The BSC clear code SERLEV measurement counters are divided into three classes. Request, success and failure counters together characterise the quality of service. All counters are given on the BTS basis. Signalling charts are drawn with the accuracy of message interface.

measurement_index.name: MS Speed Detection
measurement_index.description:
MS Speed Detection Measurement (M058) is related to software application BSS6083 MS Speed Detection. The purpose of this measurement is to collect information from the speed of the MS. There are three different speed classes in the measurement. With this information, you can find slow moving and fast moving MSs. The information is collected for each BTS.

Note that the MS speed statistics is collected only from the TCHs. The speed classes in PAFILE (BSC Control Parameter File) are connected with two following BSC-specific parameters (examples included):
- Upper limit of MS speed class 1 : 10 (speed 0-20 km per hour)
- Upper limit of MS speed class 2 : 30 (speed 21-60 km per hour)
- Otherwise the speed belongs to class 3 (higher than 60 km per hour)

measurement_index.name: Dual Band
measurement_index.description:
Dual Band (M059) gives information on the traffic distribution. In the measurement the Handover and Power Control (HO-PC) algorithm measures the cumulative TCH holding time of single band subscribers and of dual band subscribers. The measurement also counts the TCH reservations made by the single band and dual band subscribers. Here the TCH reservation means the starting of a HO-PC algorithm slave process in a TCH. The information is collected for each BTS.

The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH only.

measurement_index.name: Load
measurement_index.description: Load measurement (M006) registers information on the peak and the average load rate of the message bus and computer units. The information is collected for the message bus and each computer unit of the BSC in question.

measurement_index.name: C/I Ratio
measurement_index.description:
C/I Ratio Measurement (M060) is to estimate the level of the potential co- and adjacent channel interference in the radio network. The interference estimation is based on the measurement results reported by the MS via the BTS. This measurement can be used by the automatic frequency planning software and by the frequency planning of the underlay-overlay network. The information is collected for each cell.

The C/I ratio measurement collects statistics on the degree of the interference by measuring traffic intensity (erlang) on a specified C/I ratio (carrier/interference) band.

measurement_index.name: Hot Spot
measurement_index.description:
Hot Spot Measurement (M061) helps you to find out the traffic distribution in a mobile communication network. With this measurement you can retrieve information that indicates the places in the network where more capacity is needed.

When locating the traffic distribution, information on the adjacent cell RX levels is needed. Therefore the traffic distribution is identified with an accuracy of the serving cell and three adjacent cells.

Three adjacent cells are combined into triplets that are used in identifying the hot spots. The selection of the cells included in these triplets is made according to the RX levels so that the three adjacent cells with the strongest signal levels are included in one triplet. The hot spot measurement indicates the traffic distribution with an accuracy of these triplets. The timing advance distribution is also included in the hot spot measurement data.

measurement_index.name: DMR
measurement_index.description:
DMR measurement (M062) collects counter data from radio relay equipment. The counters are either signal quality counters (062000-062004) or RF Input level min/max counters (062005-062006).

The measurement gives information about transmission quality in used PCM connection between a DMR and the BSC or another transmission equipment (signal quality counters) and about Radio Frequency level of a nearby Base Station (RF Input level min/max).
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: DN2
measurement_index.description:
DN2 measurement (M063) collects counter data from the DN2 equipment. The counters are signal quality counters (063000-063004).

The measurement gives information about transmission quality in used PCM connection between a DN2 and the BSC or another transmission equipment.
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: TRU/BIE
measurement_index.description:
TRU/BIE measurement (M064) collects counter data from the TRU/BIE equipment. The counters are signal quality counters (062000-062005).

The measurement gives information about transmission quality in used PCM connection between a TRU/BIE and the BSC or another transmission equipment.
Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: ET BSC
measurement_index.description:
ET BSC measurement (M065) is related to BSS7072 ET Downtime Statistics. The ET BSC measurement counters characterise the signal quality of each 2Mbit/s interface of an ET (exchange terminal) controlled by the BSC. 

The CRC counters are updated only if the CRC mode of the ET is in use.

Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: ET TCSM
measurement_index.description:
ET TCSM Measurement (M066) counters characterise the signal quality of each 2Mbit/s interface of an ET (exchange terminal) controlled by the TCSM. 

The CRC counters are updated only if the CRC mode of the ET is in use.

Not supported in standalone mcBSC.

measurement_index.name: M3UA Association Set
measurement_index.description:
M3UA Association Set Measurement (M661) The M3UA Association Set Measurement (295H/661) can be used to monitor MTP3 User Adaptation Layer (M3UA) traffic. It provides information on traffic throughput and quality of M3UA connections, as well as M3UA layer and M3UA Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP) layer traffic.

M3UA layer counters tell the payload of the SCTP connection. From the counters of the SCTP layer, the operator can follow the traffic of the SCTP layer used by M3UA association. The SCTP layer counters give the operator more accurate information on real load required for sending M3UA traffic through SCTP by including a number of retransmitted SCTP packets and SCTP header. Unavailability counters can be used for fault monitoring, for example, if the association is in ASP-INACTIVE state. The measurement is configured by using interface T2 MML command group commands.

measurement_index.name: High Speed Data
measurement_index.description: High Speed Data Measurement (M067) measures the functioning of the High Speed Circuit Switched Data (HSCSD) and 14.4 kbit/s Data Services. Counters are incremented at the HSCSD request, during the HSCSD connection, and in case of configuration changes.

measurement_index.name: TRE
measurement_index.description:
TRE measurement (M068) counters characterize the signal quality of an interface of Nokia Q1 generation transmission equipment.

The counters gathered from the near-end direction are based on the ITU-T recommendation G.826, and more detailed calculations can be made according to the recommendation.

The measurement collects the counter data for each interface..

measurement_index.name: Selective TRE
measurement_index.description:
Selective TRE Measurement (M069) counters characterize the signal quality of an interface of Nokia Q1 generation transmission equipment. Additionally, the received signal level is collected from a radio relay interface.

The counters gathered from the near-end direction are based on the ITU-T recommendation G.826, and more detailed calculations can be made according to the recommendation.

Target interfaces up to 500 for this measurement can be selected by the user.

This measurement type has been present since release S8.

measurement_index.name: Availability
measurement_index.description: Availability measurement (M007) registers information on the restart and the disconnection times of the computer units. The information is collected for each computer unit in the BSC in question.

measurement_index.name: Channel Finder
measurement_index.description:
Channel Finder Measurement (M070) registers statistics on cells which have not been defined as adjacent cells but which are among those six neighbouring cells that the MS receives best. This measurement type collects one block of results for each BTS.

One block (cell) of result contains six counters:
- Average strength of the downlink signal
- BCCH + BSIC
- Standard deviation (sum of squares of signal strengths)
- Three sample counters

measurement_index.name: MS Capability Indication
measurement_index.description:
MS Capability Indication measurement (M071) will provide BTS-specific information on the capabilities of the mobile stations. In this measurement, the mobile stations are separated into groups based on the following features: revision level, supported frequency band, multislot, DTM and SAIC capability.

The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH only.

measurement_index.name: Packet Control Unit
measurement_index.description:
PCU measurement (M072) gives BTS-level information on the functions in the Packet Control Unit (PCU).

The counters of this measurement give information on the different phases of temporary block flows (TBF), including allocation requests, establishments, reallocations and, finally, TBF releases. A set of counters is triggered in each of these phases. Most of the counters are provided for
uplink and downlink TBFs separately.

Furthermore, this measurement contains counters for the number of radio link control (RLC) data blocks and bad frame indications during the measurement period. These counters are available for coding schemes CS1 and CS2 in uplink and downlink separately. Another group of counters is provided for GPRS signalling transactions, such as paging and immediate assignment, as well as for certain failure situations.

All the counters are updated to the normal area object of the BTS unless otherwise stated in the counter descriptions.

measurement_index.name: RLC Blocks per TRX
measurement_index.description:
RLC Blocks per TRX measurement (M073) provides TRX-specific information on data throughput quality based on the RLC/MAC blocks. The information can be used for the parameterisation of TRX capacity.

The PCU Frame Handler (PFH) protocol object updates the counters.

measurement_index.name: Frame Relay
measurement_index.description:
Frame Relay measurement (M074) provides bearer channel and Permanent Virtual Connection (PVC) - specific information on the proper working of the frame relay between the PCU and the SGSN.

Counters 074071-074202 are PCU2 specific counters.

This measurement is not supported for the interfaces of mcBSC configured with PCUM unit.

measurement_index.name: Defined Adjacent Cell
measurement_index.description:
Defined Adjacent Cell Measurement (M075) provides BTS level information on the signal levels of the defined adjacent cells. It gives the average signal levels as well as a means of calculating the standard deviation of the signal level of each defined neighbouring cell. Furthermore, it provides the counters for the C/I ratio for each serving cell/defined adjacent cell pair. These counters give the number of samples in each of the user-defined C/I ratio classes. You can use the interference matrix generated with this measurement for automated planning.

The object level of this measurement is the serving cell. For the signal level of serving cell, the counters for calculating the average signal level as well as the standard deviation of the signal level are provided.

For the defined adjacent cells, one block of results contains six counters:
- average strength of the downlink signal
- BSIC+BCCH
- sum of the squares of the signal strengths (for standard deviation calculation)
- three sample counters for C/I values

This measurement is optional.

This measurement type has been present since release S10.

measurement_index.name: Dynamic Abis
measurement_index.description:
Dynamic Abis Measurement (M076) provides information on the usage of EDAP both in uplink and downlink directions.

The counters shall also be updated in case of Remote DAP.

measurement_index.name: FER
measurement_index.description:
FER Measurement (M077) registers information on the speech quality in the Radio interface.

The FER Measurement provides the uplink frame erasure rate (UL FER) from each codec of each TRX in the BTS. This provides a more realistic measure of voice quality in the system than the bit error ratio (BER)-based RxQuality measurement.

Additionally, the downlink frame erasure rate (DL FER) is estimated using the correlation between the UL FER and UL BER values and applying these to the DL BER values. Both the UL FER and actual or estimated DL FER values are reported in the FER measurement.

When the Enhanced Measurement Report is in use, actual DL FER values are available and the counters for real DL FER samples are updated instead of the counters for estimated DL FER. 

Note that the updating of FER Measurement UL and DL counters can be affected by data filtering. That is, if the UL RX Level value of a measurement report is below the set filtering value, the UL counters of the FER Measurement are not updated. Also, if the DL RX Level value is below the set filtering value, the DL counters of the FER Measurement are not updated. The data filtering is enabled and disabled with the PRFILE parameter RCS_FER_FILTER. The RX Level threshold for data filtering can be defined with the UTPFIL parameter RCS_FER_FILTER_LEVEL_PRM_C; the default value is -98 dBm.

measurement_index.name: Position-based Services
measurement_index.description:
Position-based Services Measurement (M078):
Location services in the BSC are either under the Position-based Services software and/or Lb interface to BSC software, and/or S9+ Locationing System software. Lb interface to BSC adds support for a third party's stand-alone SMLCs. The Position-based Services software adds support for an internal SMLC. The S9+ Locationing System software adds support for Nokia's own GMLC-based locationing method (NSN's iGMLC CD 4.0 or later).

From a statistical point of view, location services in the BSC consist of the Location Service interface (LCS interface) and an internal SMLC. The LCS interface handles general tasks related to location services in the BSC. The internal SMLC locates the subscriber and/or valid mobile equipment using conventional GPS or cell identification + TA method. The LCS interface collects information from locationing services in the BSC to be recorded into Position-based Services Measurement.

measurement_index.name: Coding Scheme
measurement_index.description:
Coding Scheme Measurement (M079) provides information about the amount of data transferred to uplink and downlink directions using the different EGPRS modulation and coding schemes (MCS) and GPRS coding schemes CS-3 and CS-4. The transferred data is represented on the radio link control (RLC) block level. The payloads carried by the RLC blocks using different coding schemes are shown in the table "Data amounts in radio blocks using different modulation and coding schemes". The measurement also has counters for different cases of invalid RLC blocks as well as RLC block retransmissions. The object level of this measurement is the BTS, modulation and coding schemes used, and the coverage area (normal or extended).

Because the MCS information is not available for radio blocks having bad header information, these blocks are reported on a dummy MCS identifier MCS-0. Other counters are updated on their respective modulation and coding scheme ranging from MCS-1 to MCS-9. CS-3 and CS-4 counters are updated on coding scheme identifiers 11 and 12, respectively. 

The counters 079000-079009 are updated both for the normal and the extended areas.

measurement_index.name: OSI/X.25
measurement_index.description: OSI measurement (M008) can measure how the connection between the BSC and the NMS functions.

measurement_index.name: Reversed Hunting
measurement_index.description:
Reversed Hunting (M089) collects information on each used A interface pool. 
The route between the MSC and the BSS may not support all types of traffic (for example, HSCSD or Half Rate). In principle this has been managed so that the MSC selects the correct terrestrial circuit from the circuit pool which supports the type of circuit needed for the connection. With Reversed A interface Circuit Allocation, the BSS directly allocates the needed circuit on the basis of the call type.

The counters show the availability of the circuits in the pool and the number of call attempts for the different types of calls.

measurement_index.name: Quality of Service
measurement_index.description: Quality of Service (QoS) measurement (M090) provides information about TBF allocations and their durations, number of transferred RLC blocks, dropped LLC PDUs, and the average DL flow rate for each priority class. The priority classes are based on combinations of GPRS delay class and GPRS precedence class values, and they are used in priority-based scheduling. The object levels of this measurement are the different priority classes on each segment. There are four priority classes in the uplink direction and three priority classes in the downlink direction.

measurement_index.name: Non-BCCH Layer Offset
measurement_index.description:
Non-BCCH Layer Offset Measurement (M092) is an offset margin is used to estimate the signal level of the non-BCCH frequency layer of a segment with the common BCCH on the BCCH frequency layer. This margin is defined as a parameter called non_BCCH_layer_offset (M092). This parameter is also used with the Multi BCF feature to compensate the known output power difference between the various base station site types.

The user is able to regulate the value of the respective parameter on the basis of the non-BCCH layer offset measurement results.

The measurement contains 83 counters. These include counters for absolute offset values from -40 dB to +40 dB in 1 dB steps. All samples that are below -40dB are collected into a separate counter. The samples that indicate a difference greater than 40 dB are also collected in a separate counter.

The samples for the measurement are collected at the SACCH signalling rate from each MS with an ongoing call in a non-BCCH frequency BTS. When defining the signal level differences, the BSC takes into account the used power levels to establish an accurate value of difference between the BCCH frequency and the non-BCCH frequency.

The statistics are collected BTS-specifically in every BTS that is on the non-BCCH frequency band of a segment utilizing the Common BCCH Control feature.

The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH only.

measurement_index.name: UTRAN Handover Adjacent Cell
measurement_index.description:
UTRAN Handover Adjacent Cell measurement (M093) of the BSC collects statistics about the distribution of inter-system handovers between different cells. It contains counters for handover attempts and successful handovers from GSM to WCDMA RAN and vice versa, as well as from TD-SCDMA RAN to GSM. The measurement also has separate counters for handover failures due to lack of resources.

The counters are collected separately for each serving cell on the GSM side. For each serving cell, there are counters for 64 WCDMA RAN or TD-SCDMA RAN neighbour cells and overflow counters (093256 - 093258) that are updated whenever WCDMA RAN or TD-SCDMA RAN handover events occur and the preceding counters for the 64 cells are already in use.

This measurement is similar to Handover Adjacent Cell Measurement, but the scope is limited to inter-system handovers.

In shifting from 3G to 2G inter-system handover, cell level statistics is not possible because of 3GPP standards, which recognise only the PLMN + LAC + SAC identification of the 3G source cell. That is why the counters (093259 - 093290) and (093547 - 093578) are not valid when shifting from 3G to 2G inter-system handover.

This measurement is optional and it is related to BSS10101 GSM-WCDMA Interworking and BSS30315 TD-SCDMA Incoming HO Support. When only the latter is active, the counters for handover attempts and successful handovers from GSM to WCDMA RAN are not updated.

measurement_index.name: UTRAN Neighbouring Cell Signal Level
measurement_index.description:
UTRAN neighbouring cell signal level measurement (M094) provides information on the signal levels of a WCDMA RAN cell in the neighbourhood of a GSM serving cell. The measurements are performed by the dual mode (WCDMA/GSM) MSs, which are attached to a GSM cell.

The measurement classifies the signal level values in three classes, according to the two user-defined class boundaries.

The counters of this measurement are updated on TCH only, and based on signal levels of WCDMA RAN cells only.

measurement_index.name: GPRS Cell Re-selection
measurement_index.description: GPRS Cell Re-selection Measurement (M095) collects information about the source and target cell, the number of cell re-selection attempts for various causes, the number of successful NCCR procedures, and the number of failures for various failure reasons.

measurement_index.name: Enhanced Quality of Service
measurement_index.description:
Enhanced Quality of Service Measurement (M097) collects statistics on packet flow context (PFC) procedures, data transfer, and quality control.
 
The only supported traffic class (TC) values are:
Interactive TC+THP1 - 1
interactive TC+THP2 - 2 
interactive TC+THP3 - 3 
background               - 5 

The possible values for the allocation/retention priority (ARP) are 1...3.
 
Counters 097047 - 097049 are optional. They require a valid licence for Packet Data Optimisation Package.

measurement_index.name: Gb over IP
measurement_index.description:
Gb over IP (M098) enables the use of IP (Internet Protocol) in Gb interface between PCU and SGSN. 

The Gb over IP measurement registers the data related to the Gb over IP feature. The information is collected from every Network Service Virtual Link (NS-VL) identified with NS-VL ID and NSE (Network Service Entity) ID.

measurement_index.name: Total FEP
measurement_index.description:
Total FEP Measurement (M099) is an optional call control measurement, which is related to the Automated Planning Enhancements.

In the total FEP Measurement, there is a separate set of counters for each BTS. These counters collect the cumulated sum of frame erasure probability (FEP) values for a certain serving cell - neighbouring cell pair during a measurement period. The measurement includes separate counters for co-channel and adjacent channel interference. The counters can collect cumulative FEP values of up to 100 adjacent cells.

On the basis of the information collected with these counters, an interference matrix can be created that specifies the cost of putting a group of cells on the same frequency..

Notes: In NetAct, FEP Measurement is splitted into 2 measurements "Total FEP, Adjacencies" and "Total FEP, Header".

measurement_index.name: Traffic
measurement_index.description: BSC traffic measurement (M001) registers information related to the stand alone dedicated control channels (SDCCH) and traffic channels (TCH). The BSC traffic measurement counters are divided into different classes. There are counters regarding the number of attempts to seize TCHs and SDCCHs, successful calls, lengths of the queue, the reasons for Failures and GPRS territory counters. This measurement collects one set of results for each BTS. Signalling charts are drawn with the accuracy of message interface.

measurement_index.name: DFCA
measurement_index.description:
DFCA measurement (M100) collects statistics on the performance of the DFCA. The data is collected at BTS level for each connection type (FR/EFR, HR, 14.4, AMR FR, AMR HR) separately.

When WB-AMR FR codec is in use, AMR FR codec is used in updating counters instead of the WB-AMR FR codec. Separation between WB-AMR FR and AMR FR is not necessary, because the air interface channel coding and the C/I conditions are the same for both of them.

The measurement includes counters for recording the number of DFCA assignments on each C/I level in proportion to the target C/I level, both uplink and downlink. In the same way the statistics on the DFCA estimate amounts are collected: there are separate counters for each most restrictive C/I value in relation to the target C/I value, uplink and downlink.

There are also counters for calculating:
- the total number of successful DFCA assignments
- the number of successful DFCA assignments in high MCMU load situation
- the number of soft blocked DFCA assignments due to C/I and C/N thresholds

measurement_index.name: DFCA Assignment
measurement_index.description: DFCA Assignment measurement (M101) collects statistics on usage of DFCA channels at BTS level. It consists of counters for combinations of DFCA MA list and MAIO and the corresponding assignment counters. The assignment counters are updated whenever the corresponding MA list and MAIO are used in a DFCA assignment.

measurement_index.name: BSC-BSC
measurement_index.description: BSC-BSC measurement (M102) collects statistics on the inter-BSC communication related to DFCA functionality. The measurement level is BSC, and the measurement objects are identified with a signalling point code (SPC). The counters of this measurement record information on average and peak delay between the Radio Resource Managers in separate BSCs.

measurement_index.name: WPS
measurement_index.description:
WPS Measurement (M103) is related to the Wireless Priority Service (WPS). This measurement is optional (licence-based).

With the counters of WPS Measurement, the user can monitor the performance of traffic channel allocation and queuing algorithms in granting priority access to WPS users.

measurement_index.name: IMSI-based Handover
measurement_index.description:
IMSI-Based Handover (M104) is like a mobile subscriber in a home or visited network can be commanded to measure selectively only cells of specified PLMN areas cells and to make handover accordingly to those specified (home or authorised) PLMNs. The input for the selective measurement control is the PLMN code that is included in the IMSI of the subscriber.

The IMSI-Based Handover measurement is a BTS-level measurement collecting statistics on the IMSI-based HO attempts and failures for each Authorised Network (ANE). There are separate counters for GSM and UTRAN networks.

IMSI-Based Handover supports also software product deactivation which is done automatically when a software product licence has expired. It has been done by changing the state of cell level activation parameters from enabled to disabled.

measurement_index.name: PS DTM
measurement_index.description: PS DTM Measurement (M105) is a BTS-level measurement collecting statistics on Dual Transfer Mode (DTM). It mainly collects network-initiated DTM call establishment information and PS connection-related information of a DTM call.

measurement_index.name: CS DTM
measurement_index.description: CS DTM Measurement (M106) is a BTS-level measurement collecting statistics on Dual Transfer Mode (DTM). It mainly collects MS-initiated DTM call establishment information and CS connection-related information of a DTM call..

measurement_index.name: AMR RX Quality
measurement_index.description:
AMR RX Quality Measurement (M107) collects statistics of received signal quality both in uplink and downlink directions for each AMR bitrate. The information is collected from each transceiver (TRX) separately.

The Bit Error Ratio (BER) based signal quality counters correspond to the eight RX Quality bands, as defined in 3GPP TS 45.008, both in uplink and downlink directions. The counters are updated by the RX Quality values as measured by the MS (downlink) and BTS (uplink) and reported in the radio link measurement messages. The RX Quality reports are collected on the traffic channels (TCHs). 

The counters that are related to Adaptive Multi Rate (AMR) give information about the distribution of the received signal quality using the different AMR bitrates. There are separate uplink and downlink counters for each RX quality band 0..7 and for full rate as well as for half rate.
